rules: Three beats per letter, same order every time: SEE (the letter shape becomes one picture), SAY (one English hook word), SEAL (one Hebrew example word from data/vocab/words.json that the same picture can show).
Word: a noun record in words.json, not hidden, frequencyRank <= 1500, pointing and gloss copied from the record, first letter (last letter for the five final forms) is the letter.
Sound claims are machine-checked per tradition against data/pronunciation/consonants.json; where a tradition differs or the hook is only a spelling cue, the perTradition line says so.
Story: at most 14 words, contains the hook, the word's transliteration and its gloss.
Picture concepts come from data/letters/mnemonics.json; changes are listed in risk.
No Hebrew is typed in the source table; nothing here is proofread by a native speaker.

perTradition.sephardi: Same sound: silent / a glottal stop between vowels (uh-oh)

letters.name: Chet

picture.idea: A closed gate at the edge of a loch (a lake), with a jug of milk standing at the gate.

sound.line: A scrape from the throat, like the ch in loch said the Scottish way. Not lock, not the ch of chair.

perTradition.israeli: Same sound: ch as in Bach / loch (back-of-throat, no English chair sound)
perTradition.sephardi: Differs: pharyngeal [ħ], a throat sound (the ch of Bach / loch is the Israeli merged value). Strict Sephardi reading uses a deeper throat sound; the loch scrape is the common Israeli value.
perTradition.ashkenazi: Same sound: ch as in Bach / loch (back-of-throat, no English chair sound); the pharyngeal is seldom observed in practice

Sephardi differs: see perTradition.
